text: Found it: in `Interval.fromISO`, `DateTime.fromISO` throws when `Settings.throwOnInvalid` is true, so the `<start>/<duration>` and `<duration>/<end>` branches never run. Fixing now.
`parseDigits` returns `NaN`. When `parseInt(str, 10)` is NaN it builds a string from the non-Latin digit mappings (empty if there are no digits) and returns `parseInt("", 10)`, which is `NaN`.

Fixed in src/interval.js. `Interval.fromISO` now wraps each `DateTime.fromISO` call in try/catch so that, when `Settings.throwOnInvalid` is true, a duration endpoint (e.g. "2016-05-25T09:00/P1D" or "P1D/2016-05-25T09:00") falls through to the `Duration.fromISO` branch instead of throwing. Verified: all three ISO forms parse correctly with throwOnInvalid on and off; invalid input still throws InvalidIntervalError. Full suite: 892 passed, only the 2 pre-existing ICU/locale failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js remain (unchanged).
#1 is fixed (done). #4: in progress, ETA ~5 min.
#1 is fixed (done). #4: fix applied, running the full test suite to verify — ETA ~3 min.

#4 is fixed: `objToLocalTS` in src/impl/util.js now uses `setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)` instead of subtracting 1900 from the year, which had pushed dates past Feb 28 of year 100 into March (year 2000 is a leap year, year 100 is not). Verified: `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 2 })` is 0100-01-02, `DateTime.fromISO("0100-01-02").minus({ day: 2 })` is 0099-12-31, and a sweep of plus/minus days over years 0–200 matches the reference. Full suite: 892 passed, same 2 pre-existing ICU failures.

After all the `example(...)` calls, `demo` joins the accumulated `examples` array into an HTML table (`"" + examples.join("") + "
"`), wraps it in a heading/paragraph, and assigns the whole string to `document.body.innerHTML`.
`latn` — `digitRegex` falls back to `numberingSystems[numberingSystem || "latn"]` when `numberingSystem` is missing.

It sets the internal `defaultZone` to `null` (so `Settings.defaultZone` falls back to `LocalZone.instance`).
It's abstract: `Zone`'s `type` getter just throws a `ZoneIsAbstractError`; concrete subclasses override it to return their type string (e.g. "local", "iana", "fixed").
`zone` becomes `new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z)` — a fixed-offset zone built from the parsed offset.
Hour 24 is valid only when the other time fields are zero: `hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0` (otherwise `integerBetween(hour, 0, 23)` must hold).
